product_name: Iowa Environmental Mesonet CONUS NEXRAD N0Q base reflectivity (NOAA WSR-88D) inside its domain + ECCC North American Radar Composite 1km rain (RADAR_1KM_RRAI, mm/h) / snow (RADAR_1KM_RSNO, cm/h) / precipitation type (Radar_1km_SfcPrecipType) outside it + EUMETNET OPERA EU DBZH composite (CC BY 4.0) in remaining radar gaps + NOAA GFS translucent model estimates (public domain) in verified radar gaps only
variable: N0Q base reflectivity dBZ (IEM domain gaps); ECCC precipitation-rate rain (mm/h)/snow (cm/h) mapped to dBZ through the ECCC 14-color class rates with the NWS Z=300R^1.4 equivalence (equal ECCC colors = equal severity = equal dBZ for rain and snow); ECCC SfcPrecipType gates snow-blue rendering. One 5-75 dBZ key for rain + 8-step blue snow ramp at matched severity.
units: dBZ key: IEM/OPERA measured; ECCC Z-R estimated equivalents
spatial_resolution_source: IEM ~1km CONUS mosaic 5-min (native rendering); ECCC 1km rain/snow/type 6-min (rain rates -> estimated dBZ via NWS Z=300R^1.4; snow classes cm/h -> snow rows directly)
spatial_resolution_rendered: 1800x1175 canvas over lon [-93.0,-73.5], lat [40.5,49.5] (mean-value binning, no upsampling of source precision)
missing_data_treatment: ECCC type-gated (SfcPrecipType snow -> blue ramp; other types -> dBZ key) where RADAR_COVERAGE_*.INV is transparent; IEM N0Q fills ECCC gaps natively (type undifferentiated); 10-px cross-fade on the coverage edge; radar-only composite (no cloud underlay, no model fill); transparent elsewhere; never zero-filled.
shoreline_mask: assets/great_lakes_watermask.png — shared NOAA medium-resolution shoreline water mask (nautical-chart compilation, mean-high-water datum; snapped + polygonized once, full vertex precision, antialiased). Overlay alpha is multiplied by this mask and edge RGB is bled into transparent pixels (anti-fringe for bilinear clients), so every product shares one shoreline.

legend_scale_html: Precipitation intensity (NEXRAD N0Q base reflectivity, dBZ, OBSERVED radar echo): LOWEST 5 Very Light cyan/blue (drizzle, mist) → Light greens (~20-30: light rain/snow) → Moderate dark green (~30-40: steady rain/snow) → Heavy yellow/orange (~40-50: heavy rain) → Severe red (~50-60: severe storms, hail possible) → Intense magenta/purple (~60-70: violent storms, large hail) → HIGHEST+ 70+ Extreme white (destructive hail, debris). Same dBZ always shows the same color in every season — rain, snow, lake-effect snow, thunderstorms. No echo (no precipitation) stays see-through so the map underneath shows. Measurement types differ by source: IEM N0Q and OPERA are MEASURED reflectivity (dBZ); ECCC rain colors are ESTIMATED dBZ equivalents converted from rain rates via Z=300R^1.4 (ECCC publishes mm/h, not dBZ — high-rate classes saturate near ~57 dBZ, so ECCC never paints the white extreme row); ECCC snow rows are snow-rate classes in cm/h (official 14-class scale, not dBZ); pale-tinted colors are GFS MODEL estimates (6-h mean rates, snow at 10:1 snow-to-liquid ratio), never radar. ECCC snow echoes render blue ONLY where SfcPrecipType classifies snow (or the snow product alone echoes; mixed/freezing rain render on the dBZ key). Snow rows are ECCC snow-rate classes in cm/h (official 14-class scale); GFS snow ranks water-equivalent rate at 10:1 SLR on the same bands.

na_bounds.note: Authoritative common geography for the four North American live layers (precipitation_na, air_temperature_na, cloud_cover_na, wind_na). Every NA builder bins its own source grid onto this exact canvas, so the four overlays align in Google Earth. Degrees per pixel: 0.05 x 0.05 (square). This boundary is a bounding extent enclosing the buffered landmass; it does not imply valid source data everywhere — areas without valid source data stay transparent.
